title: Declared the only possible source
question: Which suppliers hold the most in contracts awarded on the ground that only they can do the work, and with which departments?
finding: 850 contracts worth $1.87 billion were awarded as sole source to 583 suppliers since July 2018. Public Health accounts for 29% of the value and Airport Commission for 19%. The largest holders: Alstom Transport USA Inc ($219.5 million, Airport Commission); Curascript Specialty Distribution ($98.5 million, Public Health); Low Income Investment Fund ($67.7 million, Department of Early Childhood); BEUMER Lifecycle Management LLC ($65.3 million, Airport Commission).
how: Contracts in the Supplier Contracts table that started on or after 1 July 2018 and whose purchasing rule says "sole source", "no other source", proprietary software or equipment that only its maker may service, or the Health Department’s sole-source list, grouped by prime contractor. Other public bodies are left out. "Paid" is payments under those rules in the payment file.
limits: A sole-source award is valid when the Office of Contract Administration, or the Health Commission for the Health Department’s list, accepts the written reason. Train parts, licensed software and hospital equipment often do have one maker. The record gives the rule, not the reason, so a weak justification looks the same here as a sound one; the waiver forms held by the Office of Contract Administration would show the difference. The paid figures count payments issued in fiscal 2019 or later, which is read from the voucher number and not from the year the file lists a line under; $1.08 billion that the whole payment file lists under those years was issued earlier and is left out.
